title: Karniyarik (Vegetarian)
subtitle: Turkish stuffed aubergine with spiced tomato and pine nuts
excerpt: Aubergines split and filled with a spiced tomato, onion and pine nut mixture, then baked until the skin wrinkles and the filling caramelises at the edges. Serve warm or at room temperature.
sourceNotes: Karniyarik is a classic Turkish stuffed aubergine dish. This version replaces the traditional lamb mince with pine nuts and extra vegetables.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare the stuffing a day ahead and refrigerate. Fill and bake the aubergines fresh.

content.text: Karniyarik means split belly. The aubergine is slit and opened wide, then stuffed generously. The skin needs to be tender before you fill it, so do not rush the first roast.
Heat the oven to 190C. Rub the aubergines all over with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil. Place in a roasting tin and roast for 25 minutes until the skin begins to wrinkle.
Meanwhile, warm the remaining olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic, green pepper and pine nuts. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring often.
Add the tomatoes, tomato puree, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes break down. Remove from the heat and stir in the parsley.
Remove the roasted aubergines from the oven. Cut a deep slit along the length of each one, leaving the ends intact. Gently open the slit wide with a spoon.
Spoon the filling generously into each aubergine. Mix the tinned tomatoes and water and pour around the aubergines in the tin.
Return to the oven and bake for 30 minutes until the filling is caramelised and the sauce is thick. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The aubergine flesh is too firm to open easily.
items.cause: The initial roast was not long enough.
items.fix: Return to the oven for another 10 minutes before splitting. The skin should give when pressed.

items.symptom: The filling spills out during baking.
items.cause: Too much filling was added or the slit was not deep enough to hold it.
items.fix: Press the filling in firmly and cup the sides of the aubergine around it before putting back in the oven.

items.symptom: The sauce in the tin has burned dry.
items.cause: Too little liquid was added around the aubergines.
items.fix: Add another 100 ml of water part way through if the tin looks dry. Cover loosely with foil.
